The client's place in Setup

Every picture is the real platform with the change drawn into the live page. Nothing here is built yet. The choices to make are gathered at the bottom.

1 · The client gets its own group on the rail

Today

One rail item, Getting started, and three pills at the top of the page with Back, Next and Done with set-up under them.

Proposed

A group The client at the top of the rail, with three items: Profile, The shape and Forefront team. The group's heading says 2 of 3 done until all three are. A tick marks each finished one and a gold dot the one still waiting. The pills and the Back, Next and Done buttons go.

A name for the first item Your choice

NameWhy
Profile RecommendedEverything on it describes the client: its name, address, mark, colours and modules. One short word, and it reads well beside The shape.
DetailsPlain, but it says nothing about colours or modules, and it is also the name of the first tab below.
IdentityFits the name, mark and colours. Modules are not part of an identity.

2 · The Profile page: three ways to lay it out

Today the name, the industry, the size, the notes, the address, the mark, the colours, the modules and archiving all sit on one long page. Each option splits them into the three you named. The mark goes with the colours, so that part is called Brand. Archiving sits at the foot of Details, behind its own question as now.

A · Tabs at the top Recommended

One tab at a time. Each part is a separate job, so the page is short, and the colours keep their Apply row right under them. If you switch tab with a colour picked but not applied, the strip at the bottom asks first, as it does when you leave the page today.

B · Three summary cards at the top

Each card shows where that part stands: the name and industry, the two colours and whether there is a mark, and how many modules are on. Press a card to open it underneath. It gives the most at a glance, but the cards take a band of the screen on every visit.

C · One page with shortcuts

Everything stays on one page, in three marked parts, with a bar at the top that jumps to each part and stays in view as you scroll. This is closest to today and the least to learn, but the page stays long.

3 · Forefront team and The office are the same page

Getting started › The office

Setup › Forefront team

They are one table drawn in two places: the same columns, the same Add, and they save to the same place. They were kept in both on purpose so the two could never disagree, not because they do different jobs.

Proposed: keep one page, called Forefront team, as the third item under The client (it is in the rail picture above), and take it out of People & access. Two small fixes ride with it. The question "Who runs the strategy office?" goes, because the page lists Forefront's people only, not the client's own office. And when adding somebody is refused, the page will say why. Today that message never shows on this page.

4 · The organisation pages: keep what only they do

The shape screen builds the tree when a client is set up. Once the client has a plan it locks, and these pages become the only place a unit or function is added, renamed, given a head or put in order. Two of them earn their place. Two do not.

PageWhat only it doesProposed
Business unitsEach unit's code, its short name in the navigation, its head and custodian, its mark, its place in the navigation, retiring it, clearing its plan. And adding or renaming a unit once the client has a plan.Keep. Divisions become headings on this page (picture below).
DivisionsTwo switches: whether a division's CEO sees the other divisions, and whether they see the group. And retiring one.Fold into Business units, with the two switches on each division's heading, and remove the page. Its note also says a division has no score and no page, which stopped being true some time ago.
FunctionsThe same as Business units, for functions. Also which unit a pillar-planning function sits under, and deleting one.Keep. Drop the Caps column: it counts capabilities filed under a function, which can no longer happen.
CapabilitiesNames, owners and custodians of capability records. No live client has one any more. Their capabilities are pillars inside the units' plans, which this page cannot see, so it shows empty. Only the demo has one, Product Mindset.Remove. The demo's one record becomes a pillar first. Whether a client has capabilities at all stays a switch on the shape screen.

Business units, with divisions as headings

Each division is a heading over its units, carrying its two switches and its menu (rename, retire). Units with no division sit under Not in a division. + Add a division sits beside + Add a business unit. Within each heading the units keep their navigation order. The rail on the left shows the whole Setup rail with everything on this page agreed.

Functions, without the Caps column

5 · The Official BU list moves to The organisation

It translates the names the client's own HR records use for departments (Distribution, Finance, Mazaya…) into the units and functions here. Four things read it:

The people fileA person's department name places them in the right unit when the file is uploaded.
Signing inSomebody not yet placed is asked where they work, from a short list built from it.
The People registerMarks a person whose department name says one place while they sit in another.
Owner pickersA department name that points nowhere is offered as an owner, for lines owned by a department rather than a person.

Nothing else does this, so it stays. It moves under The organisation because it is about where the parts of the business are, not about who may do what. It sits last there, after Functions. On the demo none of the ten names points anywhere yet, which is why it looks unused.

The grey "Key Measures" in your screenshot

Today

Option 1 · the word shows as a real word

That box is empty. The grey word is what the pages say when nothing is typed, and for this client it is Key Measures. That word was saved for the whole client on the old Terminology page. It is not the product's default, which is Key Objectives. Since Terminology went, nothing shows that word or lets you change it.

FixWhat happens
1 · Show it as a real word RecommendedEach word saved on the old page is written into the boxes it applies to, in black, where you can see and change it. The grey hint then always shows the product's default. No page changes until you change a box. Clearing this one gives you Key Objectives.
2 · Clear the old wordsEvery word saved on the old page goes, so every empty box and every page reads the product's default: Key Objectives here. Any other word this client chose on that page goes back to the default too, without anyone seeing it happen.

What you would be agreeing to

  1. The client as a group at the top of the rail with three items, and the first one called Profile (or Details, or Identity).
  2. The Profile page laid out as A · tabs (recommended), B · summary cards, or C · one page with shortcuts.
  3. Forefront team kept once, as the third item under The client, and taken out of People & access.
  4. Divisions folded into Business units as headings, and its page removed.
  5. The Capabilities page removed, after the demo's one record becomes a pillar.
  6. Functions kept, without the Caps column.
  7. The Official BU list moved under The organisation, after Functions.
  8. For the grey Key Measures: fix 1, show the old words as real words (recommended), or fix 2, clear them back to the defaults.
